thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired: P1 - az2 control-plane heartbeat loss detected. Affected: routing control and KV-prefetch paths. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/az-controlplane-loss

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to oncall rota. Escalation policy: primary -> infra -> sre.

sara: acked via PagerDuty. I'm on call, joining bridge: https://calls.redwood/incident/3249998888 

raj: I'm seeing a 45% increase in request 5xxs from az2 since 09:41 UTC, and control plane heartbeats to instances in az2 stopped at 09:40:23. Control-plane metrics: `control.heartbeat.missed` spike.

marta: Confirming KV cache miss rates up, prefix cache eviction skyrocketed. Looks like control-plane heartbeats timed out, which caused routing agent to mark several nodes unhealthy.

eli: Quick checklist from runbook: 1) divert traffic off az2 2) enable emergency fallback model variant 3) scale up az3 shards if needed. I'm going to flip routing to divert mode and open a rolling drain plan.

sara: Agreed. Start divert. I will coordinate customer comms. Bryan, can you surface any customers with active incidents?

bryan-cs: AcmeCorp and DreamApp reported 502/timeout errors at 09:43. Both are in us-east with traffic routed through az2. I'm drafting a status note.

raj: Running routing divert command now.
```
# control plane routing divert
redwoodctl routing set-weight --from az2 --to az3,az1 --weights 0.0,0.7,0.3 --reason "auto-divert az2 heartbeat loss"
```

marta: Routing change applied. Confirming from routing-proxy logs: `divert: az2 -> az3: 75% of new sessions`, `az2 sessions draining`.

eli: Initiating fallback activation for latency-sensitive routes: enabling quantized-model-variant for critical tenants to reduce compute pressure while divert completes.

sara: Noting customer impact in incident bridge: "Partial degraded responses, increased latencies and 502s for some us-east customers; fallback and routing diversion in progress." :pencil:

pagerduty: PagerDuty: ack by sara. Notification: escalation halted.

raj: We're seeing control-plane reconnections attempts from az2, but heartbeat jitter remains. Killswitch on autoscaler in az2 to prevent noisy scale loops applied.

marta: Pushing a KV cache warmup for az3 to reduce cold-start errors while traffic increases.
```
# warmup curl
for s in $(cat critical_shards.txt); do curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/kv/warmup/$s; done
```

eli: Observability: 10m after divert, 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 3% for affected routes. Latency still ~200ms higher on some paths. Customers seeing improvement per Bryan.

bryan-cs: Confirmed: DreamApp says errors subsided at 09:58. AcmeCorp still sees occasional 502s but much better. Sending update to both.

sara: Good. We'll keep divert until az2 control-plane is healthy. Raj, can you run diagnostics on the NIC and hypervisor control channel in az2?

raj: On it. Early signs point to a noisy NIC firmware bug in 2 hosts causing control plane disconnects. Opening hardware ticket with provider and isolating affected hosts from routing.

kevin-oncall: I will take a handoff in 20 minutes for night oncall. Any outstanding action items for me?

sara: Handoff notes: keep routing divert active, monitor heartbeat recovery, coordinate with provider for host replacement, keep CS updates until fully recovered. I will be available on the bridge for 30 more minutes.

eli: Also add: keep fallback variant enabled for critical routes for another 30m post-recovery to avoid regressions.

raj: Provider acknowledged hardware ticket, scheduled replacement for the two faulty hosts in az2. Isolating hosts done. Control-plane heartbeats restored to most nodes at 10:12 UTC.

marta: Gradual reweighting started: `redwoodctl routing set-weight --from az2 --to az3,az1 --weights 0.2,0.6,0.2` then userside healthcheck pass.

incident-bot: System note: routing state changed, divert disabled for most services, az2 reintroduced with caution flag.

eli: Metrics look stable 30m post-reintroduction. 5xxs flatlined to baseline, latency back within SLO for most tenants.

bryan-cs: Customer update sent: "Traffic restored and degraded behavior resolved, continued monitoring. Follow-up postmortem will be shared."

sara: I'm closing active pager with a handoff to kevin. Will draft a short blameless postmortem and point to runbook gaps (firmware checks in provider on our checklist).

kevin-oncall: Ack taking over. Thanks all. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved: P1 -> mitigated. Timeline: start 09:40 UTC, divert started 09:45, partial recovery 10:12, stable 10:45. Postmortem assigned to: raj, marta, eli, sara.

sara: Thanks team. Follow-up items: (1) add NIC firmware check to preflight, (2) add faster warmup path for kv caches during divert, (3) review routing weight defaults for rapid-divert scenarios. I'll create the incident ticket and link logs. :white_check_mark:"
